A 25-year-old male with a history of polysubstance abuse is transported to the emergency department
after being discovered unconscious on the street. He is minimally responsive, even to painful stimuli,
and unable to provide a coherent history or emergency contacts. His vital signs show: temperature
99.3°F (35.6°C), blood pressure 115/52 mmHg, pulse 43/min, and respiratory rate 11/min. Following a
urine toxicology screen, treatment is administered. Shortly after receiving the treatment, the patient
develops rhythmic extremity contractions and bites his tongue. Which therapeutic agent was most likely
administered? Answer Choices: (A) Fomepizole (B) Flumazenil (C) Sodium bicarbonate (D) Dextrose
(E) Physostigmine (F) Glucagon (G) N-acetylcysteine (H) Naloxone (I) Thiamine (J) Pralidoxime
 A. Dextrose

B. Pralidoxime

E. Physostigmine
